items.title: Information Barrier and MNPI Policy
items.text:
Information Barrier and MNPI Policy
Effective: Wednesday, July 15, 2026
Owner: Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer
Applies to: All Halcyon Ridge Capital employees, contractors and temporary staff

Purpose
Halcyon Ridge runs advisory, lending, wealth and trading businesses under one roof. This policy sets out how we keep material non-public information (MNPI) inside the people who need it, so that we protect our clients, our counterparties and the firm's licenses. If you are unsure whether something is covered, assume it is and call the Control Room.

What Counts as MNPI
Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important to a decision to buy, sell or hold a security, or if it would likely move the price. It is non-public until it has been broadly disseminated, for example through a press release or regulatory filing, and the market has had time to absorb it. Typical examples include pending mergers, acquisitions, tender offers or divestitures; unannounced earnings or guidance; significant financing, restructuring or credit events; major customer wins or losses; senior management changes; and material litigation or labor actions. Valuation ranges, bid levels, deal timing and the identity of parties in a live mandate are always MNPI.

Deal Codenames
Every advisory mandate receives a codename from the Control Room at engagement. Codenames must be used in all internal communications, calendar invites, file names and system entries. Do not pair a codename with a ticker, company name or obvious descriptor outside the approved deal-team channel or data room.

Wall-Crossing Procedure
No one may be brought over the wall without prior Control Room approval. The deal lead submits a wall-crossing request naming the individual, the business reason and the expected duration. Compliance reviews for conflicts, including outside brokerage accounts and recent personal trading, and records the approval. The crossed individual receives a written acknowledgment that they now hold MNPI and must not trade in, recommend or discuss the affected securities. Wall crossings are logged and reviewed monthly; the deal lead must notify the Control Room when a person no longer needs access.

Restricted and Watch Lists
The Watch List is confidential to Compliance and lists issuers about which the firm may hold MNPI; it is used for surveillance and is never distributed. The Restricted List is circulated firm-wide and prohibits proprietary trading, solicited client trading, research commentary and personal trading in listed issuers. Additions are made by the Control Room and are effective immediately. OMS pre-trade controls block restricted names; overrides require written Compliance sign-off.

Where Deal Discussion Is Allowed
Live transactions may only be discussed in the private, Compliance-administered deal-team channel for that codename, in the approved virtual data room, and on calls or in meetings limited to wall-crossed staff. Deal discussion is prohibited in public channels such as #general, #trading-desk, #random or #ma-team, in direct messages with anyone not crossed, and in elevators, the cafeteria or any public setting. Personal email and messaging apps may never be used.

Trading Desk Separation
Traders, sales traders, quant analysts and trading associates must never receive MNPI. Advisory staff must not take calls from, share screens with or sit with Trading personnel on deal matters. If a trader believes they have inadvertently received MNPI, they must stop all activity in the relevant name, tell no one else, and contact the Control Room immediately.

Escalation
Report suspected leaks, unauthorized access or accidental disclosure to Marcus Bell or the Compliance team in #compliance with no deal details, or by phone. Compliance will assess whether the issuer should be restricted and whether a broader review is required. Good-faith reporting is protected from retaliation.

Disciplinary Consequences
Breaches of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, clawback of compensation, and referral to regulators and law enforcement. Insider trading and tipping carry personal civil and criminal liability. Managers who fail to supervise are accountable as well.

Questions
Direct questions to the Control Room. This policy is reviewed annually.

items.title: Project Falcon - Wall-Crossing Memo and Deal Team
items.text:
Project Falcon - Wall-Crossing Memo and Deal Team
STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL - CONTAINS MNPI
Date: Monday, August 3, 2026
From: Elena Vasquez, Managing Director, M&A Advisory
To: Project Falcon deal team; Marcus Bell, Control Room

Mandate
Halcyon Ridge has been engaged as buy-side financial advisor to Meridian Freight Partners in connection with its proposed acquisition of Northwind Logistics Group (NYSE-listed, ticker NWLG). Indicative enterprise value is approximately $1.2B. The engagement letter was countersigned last week and the Control Room has assigned the codename Project Falcon. Use the codename in every communication, file name and calendar entry.

Deal Team (Wall-Crossed)
Elena Vasquez, Managing Director - deal lead
Tom Hargreave, Vice President - day-to-day execution, client board materials
Aisha Karim, Associate - diligence coordination, data room
Susan Harrington, Analyst - model, comps and precedent transactions

Each team member has signed the MNPI acknowledgment and completed the personal-account attestation. No one else at the firm, including other members of M&A Advisory, is to be brought in without a new request to the Control Room through me.

Control Room Contact
Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer. Any question about access, inadvertent disclosure or a request from outside the team goes to Marcus first.

Restricted List
Effective today, NWLG is added to the firm Restricted List. OMS pre-trade blocks are live for Trading, and Wealth Management cannot solicit or recommend the name. The reason for the restriction is not disclosed outside this group.

Communication Rules
All Falcon discussion happens only in #project-falcon, the Falcon data room, or on calls limited to the four of us plus Meridian and its advisors. Not in #ma-team, not in DMs, not over lunch. Printed materials stay locked when you are away from your desk.

Timeline
Target public announcement: Monday, November 2, 2026. Interim milestones (diligence close-out, financing commitments, fairness opinion, board approvals) will be tracked in the workplan Aisha is circulating in the data room.

Please confirm receipt in #project-falcon.

Elena

Data room update on Northwind: FY25 EBITDA came in at $142M, a touch above the CIM, and top-5 customers are 38% of revenue. Also flagging a pending labor dispute at their Ohio depots, docs are in folder 4.3, still waiting on counsel's read on exposure.

Thanks Aisha. That 38% concentration is going to come up with Meridian's board for sure, so can you put together a churn analysis on the top-5 (contract terms, renewal dates, any history of volume drops) by Friday? Susan can help pull the revenue cuts.

Just off with Meridian: they're comfortable with a $1.15-1.25B range, and we're still targeting announcement on Nov 2. Reminder for everyone, nothing about Falcon leaves this channel, no DMs, no #ma-team, no hallway chat. Sync tomorrow at 7.

items.title: Project Falcon diligence sync
items.text:
Elena Vasquez: Okay, it's the four of us, door's closed. Quick recap from last night: Meridian is comfortable with $1.15 to $1.25 billion and we're holding November 2 for announcement. Let's go workstream by workstream. Aisha, commercial first.
Aisha Karim: Commercial is mostly done. The churn analysis on the top-5 customers is in the data room. Three of the five are on multi-year contracts with renewals after 2028, one renews next spring, and one is month-to-month after a volume drop last year. That last one is the soft spot.
Tom Hargreave: That's the one Meridian's board will zero in on. Can we quantify the downside if it walks?
Susan Harrington: I ran it in the model. Losing that customer entirely takes about $11M off EBITDA on a run-rate basis. At the midpoint multiple it's still inside the range, but it pushes us toward the low end.
Elena Vasquez: Good. Put that as a sensitivity page in the board deck, not buried in the appendix. Legal?
Aisha Karim: Meridian's counsel has finished the contract review. Two change-of-control clauses in customer agreements, both with consent rights rather than termination rights. Counsel is comfortable but wants the consents as a covenant, not a closing condition.
Tom Hargreave: Fine with me. Northwind will push back if we try to make it a condition anyway.
Elena Vasquez: Agreed. Labor dispute in Ohio, where are we?
Aisha Karim: Northwind's employment counsel says it's a grievance over overtime and scheduling at the Ohio depots, covering a few hundred drivers and warehouse staff. No strike authorization vote yet. Their estimate is a settlement of a few million plus higher wage costs going forward.
Susan Harrington: I've modeled a two percent wage step-up at those depots. It's around $3M a year. Small, but I'd want a specific indemnity or an escrow if it escalates before signing.
Elena Vasquez: Raise that with Meridian's counsel tomorrow. Tom, I also want a line in the disclosure schedule review so we see exactly how Northwind describes it. Financing next.
Tom Hargreave: Meridian's lenders are sending a revised commitment letter Monday. Term loan plus a revolver, with a bridge backstop. Leverage lands around four and a half times on Susan's adjusted EBITDA. The lenders want the labor sensitivity in their model too.
Elena Vasquez: Share only what Meridian authorizes and run it through their side, not ours. Our lending desk has no role here, and I don't want anyone on Brian's team approached about it. Fairness opinion timing?
Susan Harrington: The board meeting to approve is penciled in for October 26. Our fairness committee needs the near-final model and the draft opinion a week ahead, so October 19 at the latest.
Elena Vasquez: Make it October 16. I want buffer for committee questions. I'll let Marcus know the committee members will need to be wall-crossed before then.
Tom Hargreave: I'll draft the request to the Control Room this week so it's not a scramble.
Elena Vasquez: Thanks. Announcement prep for November 2. Meridian's comms firm is drafting the press release and the investor presentation. We review the deal summary and the financial advisor language. Aisha, own the checklist: press release, investor call script, Q and A, and the fallback plan if there's a leak before announcement.
Aisha Karim: Will do. I'll have a first version in the data room by Monday.
Susan Harrington: Do we need anything from our side on the restricted list after announcement?
Elena Vasquez: NWLG stays restricted until Marcus clears it post-closing or post-announcement, his call. Don't assume. Last thing: I saw a calendar invite circulating with Northwind's name in it. It was Meridian's side, not ours, but check yours. Codename only.
Tom Hargreave: Already scrubbed mine.
Elena Vasquez: Good. Action items: Susan, sensitivity pages and model to the fairness committee by October 16. Aisha, labor indemnity point to counsel and announcement checklist by Monday. Tom, financing review and the Control Room request. Same time next Thursday. Thanks, everyone.
